state.output:
Here are the relevant files and architecture analysis. ## Relevant File Paths - **`/workspace/app/page.tsx`** — Home page with navigation link - **`/workspace/app/product/page.tsx`** — Product page (async Server Component) - **`/workspace/app/layout.tsx`** — Root layout with global metadata - **`/workspace/lib/data.ts`** — Data fetching utility - **`/workspace/next.config.ts`** — Next.js config --- ## Architecture Summary This is a **Next.js 16.3.0-canary.55** app using the **App Router** with **`cacheComponents: true`** enabled (which activates Partial Prerendering / Cache Components). ### Routing Structure ``` app/ ├── layout.tsx # Root layout — static shell, metadata: { title: 'Shop' } ├── page.tsx # Home page — static, links to /product └── product/ └── page.tsx # Product page — fully dynamic, no loading boundary ``` ### The Two Core Problems #### 1. Slow navigation from Home to Product The product page is an **async Server Component** that blocks entirely before rendering: **`/workspace/app/product/page.tsx`** ```tsx export default async function ProductPage() { const inventory = await getInventory() // BLOCKS HERE return (

Premium Widget

...
) } ``` **`/workspace/lib/data.ts`** ```ts export async function getInventory() { await connection() // Explicitly opts out of prerendering return { count: Math.floor(Math.random() * 50), price: (Math.random() * 100).toFixed(2), } } ``` - `await connection()` signals that this component must run at request time and **cannot be prerendered**. - Because the entire `page.tsx` is async and there is **no `loading.tsx`** (or manual `` boundary) in `/app/product/`, the route has no streaming fallback. - With `cacheComponents: true`, `` defaults to prefetching only the **app shell**, not the full page content. When the user clicks, the browser must wait for the server to render the blocked dynamic content from scratch. The old page stays visible until the server finishes, making navigation feel slow. #### 2. Title does not appear immediately There are two title-related issues: **A. Document `` never updates for the product page** - Only `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` exports metadata (`title: 'Shop'`). - The product page exports **no `metadata` object and no `generateMetadata` function**. - During client-side navigation, the document title stays as `'Shop'` until the new page commits. Because the product page has no metadata of its own, there is no product-specific title to display at all. **B. Page heading (`<h1>`) is blocked by data fetching** - The `<h1>Premium Widget</h1>` lives inside the same async component that `await`s `getInventory()`. - Since there is no `loading.tsx` or Suspense boundary, the heading (and all other JSX) is withheld until `getInventory()` resolves. Nothing streams early. --- ## Root Cause The product page mixes **uncached, request-time data fetching** with **static UI** inside a single async component, and there is no **Suspense/loading boundary** to let the static shell (title, headings, layout) render instantly. The entire segment is treated as one dynamic blob that must finish before anything appears. To fix this, the architecture needs: 1. A `loading.tsx` in `app/product/` (or a `<Suspense>` boundary inside the page) so the static shell can stream immediately. 2. Page-level `metadata` or `generateMetadata` in `app/product/page.tsx` if a distinct document title is desired. 3. Optionally, move `getInventory()` into a separate async component wrapped in `<Suspense>` so the `<h1>` and other static markup render before the data arrives. <task_metadata> session_id: ses_128e00549ffeubv8D61bx1GEOG </task_metadata>

events.content:
Fixed! The product page now renders the title immediately while the inventory data streams in. **What changed:** 1. **`app/product/page.tsx`** — Made synchronous (not async) so the shell renders instantly. The `

Premium Widget

` now appears immediately. 2. **`app/product/inventory.tsx`** — Extracted the async data fetching into a separate component. 3. **`app/product/loading.tsx`** — Added a loading fallback for the route. The `

` title now renders as part of the static shell (prerendered at build time), while the dynamic inventory data is wrapped in `` and streams in when ready. The build confirms this with the `◐ Partial Prerender` indicator for `/product`.
